faq.q: Is January a good time to rent a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, if you enjoy mild weather and fewer crowds. January averages 17°C highs and 9°C lows, with 6 hours of daily sunshine. The sea is calm, and you can cruise comfortably in a covered flybridge or cockpit. It’s not swimming weather, but it’s perfect for sightseeing along the coast.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in January?
faq.a: The Mediterranean sea temperature in January averages around 15°C. That’s too cold for most swimmers without a wetsuit, but paddleboarding or a quick dip is possible for the brave. Most January charters focus on coastal cruising and dining rather than water sports.

faq.q: Which boats are best for a January charter?
faq.a: Flybridge or enclosed-cabin boats like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offer sheltered indoor areas with heating. The Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) is another excellent choice for winter comfort. All depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: Do you offer shorter charters in winter?
faq.a: Yes. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. For longer trips, the Mangusta 80 requires a minimum 4-hour booking at €4,719 (includes a jet ski). Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What should I wear for a January boat trip?
faq.a: Layer up: a thermal base, fleece or jumper, and a windproof jacket. Even in 17°C, the sea breeze can feel cool. Bring sunglasses and sunscreen – the UV is still strong. Non-slip shoes are recommended. The boat will have a cabin or flybridge to shelter from wind.

faq.q: Can we see dolphins in January?
faq.a: Yes, dolphin sightings are possible year-round off the Marbella coast. January often sees common dolphins and bottlenose dolphins hunting near the shore. The calm winter seas make spotting easier. Your skipper will know the best areas, often near Cabopino or the Guadalmina river mouth.

faq.q: What are the best destinations for a January cruise?
faq.a: Popular routes include cruising east towards Cabopino or west to Estepona and Sotogrande. The coastline is quieter in winter, so you’ll have anchorages like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés almost to yourself. The views of La Concha mountain are particularly clear in winter air.

faq.q: How do I book a January 2028 charter?
faq.a: You can book directly via our website or WhatsApp. For Tier A boats, select your date and pay online. For larger yachts, contact us for availability and pricing. All charters include skipper, fuel, insurance, Spanish VAT, and a selection of drinks and snacks.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental weather January 2028? Winter in Marbella is mild, sunny, and far less crowded than summer. While swimming might be off the cards, coastal cruising, dolphin spotting, and waterfront dining are very much on. This guide gives you the real weather data, sea temperatures, and practical tips to decide if a January charter is worth it. All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, and every booking includes a skipper, insurance, drinks, snacks, and VAT.

January Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

Marbella enjoys a subtropical Mediterranean climate. In January, average high temperatures reach 17°C, with lows around 9°C. Sea temperature hovers at 15°C – too cool for a long swim, but fine for a quick paddle. You can expect about 6 hours of sunshine daily, with 5-6 rainy days across the month. Wind speeds are typically light, 10-15 knots, making for calm cruising conditions. The visibility is often excellent, with the Sierra Blanca mountains and La Concha peak sharply defined in the crisp winter air.

Is It Warm Enough for a Boat Trip?

Yes – if you dress appropriately. A January afternoon on the water can feel pleasant in the sun, especially on a flybridge or enclosed deck. Our larger yachts like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) have heated interiors and wind-protected areas. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers a spacious saloon with panoramic windows – perfect for watching the coast without the chill. For shorter trips, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) at €749 for 2 hours gives you a taste of winter cruising without a big commitment.

What to Expect on a January Charter

  • Scenery: Clear winter light makes the coastline and mountains photograph beautifully. La Concha often has a dusting of snow.
  • Wildlife: Dolphins are common – your skipper can take you to their favourite hunting grounds near Cabopino or the Guadalmina river.
  • Anchoring: Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are quiet in winter. You can anchor for lunch or a quiet drink.
  • Dining: Many chiringuitos and beach clubs remain open, especially in Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina. Your skipper can recommend a spot.
  • Sunset: January sunsets are early (around 6:30 PM) and spectacular, with golden light over the water.

Which Boats Are Best for Winter?

For comfort in cooler weather, choose a boat with a fully enclosed saloon or flybridge. Our fleet includes several options: the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) and its grey variant are popular for winter charters thanks to their large indoor spaces. The Azimut 58 Flybridge offers a heated helm area. For a more intimate trip, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) has a cosy cabin. If you want to combine cruising with a jet ski, the Mangusta 80 includes a jet ski free on its minimum 4-hour booking (€4,719).

January Charter Pricing

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours and go up to €2,299 for 8 hours – all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) requires a minimum 4-hour booking at €4,719, which includes a jet ski. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). There are no hidden costs.

Should You Book a January 2028 Charter?

If you’re after a quiet, scenic, and affordable way to experience the Costa del Sol from the water, January is a great choice. You’ll avoid summer crowds, enjoy lower demand (and therefore more flexible booking), and see the coastline in its most natural state. The weather is reliable – cold mornings, mild afternoons, and mostly dry. For a unique winter experience, a boat rental in Marbella in January is definitely worth it.
